svg.font-family: Inter, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Figure 3. Harvest now, decrypt later, and the two defenses against it
svg.desc: A timeline. Encrypted traffic is recorded today and stored. Later, a key is compromised or a capability arrives that breaks the key exchange. Forward secrecy defends against the first case by deleting per-message keys. Post-quantum key exchange defends against the second. A deployment timeline follows: Signal added a post-quantum key exchange in 2023, Apple shipped its post-quantum messaging protocol in 2024, Signal added a post-quantum ratchet in 2025, and Session restored forward secrecy in late 2025 after removing it in 2021.
svg.text: Figure 3: The Attack That Happens Later
An adversary who cannot read your traffic today can still record it, and wait.
TODAY
Your encrypted traffic is
recorded and stored. It cannot
be read, and it is kept anyway.
YEARS LATER
Either your long-term key is
obtained, or a capability arrives
that breaks the key exchange.
THE OLD TRAFFIC IS READ
Everything recorded in the first box becomes
readable at once, retrospectively, and there is
nothing you can do about it at that point.
Two defenses, and they address the two halves of the middle box
FORWARD SECRECY

g.text: Each message uses its own key, derived and then
discarded. The long-term key that an adversary might
seize does not reconstruct the discarded ones.
Seizing a device stops reading the archive.

svg.text: POST-QUANTUM KEY EXCHANGE

g.text: Forward secrecy does not help if the method used to
agree the keys is itself broken later. A second, quantum-
resistant exchange is mixed in alongside the classical one.
Hybrid, so it is no weaker than what it replaces.

svg.text: This stopped being theoretical while the older version of this lesson was being written

g.text: Signal adds a post-quantum key exchange for session setup.
Apple ships a post-quantum messaging protocol with ongoing rekeying, and adds contact key verification.
Signal adds a post-quantum ratchet alongside the existing two. Session restores forward secrecy, four years after removing it.

svg.text: Note the last entry. A platform's reputation is not its current specification, and a protocol can lose a property as well as gain one.
Check which version you are running, and what that version actually does.
